Class ContainerPanel

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.containers.api.slot.ContainerPanel
public final class ContainerPanel extends Object
The one-call, no-mixin registration for a panel whose slots have container parity, they appear, click, and sync on every screen that shows the player inventory (survival, creative, and every chest/furnace/modded container), default-on, opt-out per screen.

What one registration drives

// Consumer COMMON initializer (runs both sides): the slots, and where the panel sits.
ContainerPanel.define("inventory-plus:pockets")
    .at(PanelPosition.region(OutsideRegion.LEFT_ALIGN_TOP).priority(20), 7)
    .style(PanelStyle.RAISED)
    .addSlot(SlotSpec.at("pockets", MY_CATEGORY).count(9)   // slots flow and wrap to width
            .storage(player -> POCKETS.bind(player)))
    .register();

// Consumer CLIENT initializer, only for chrome or a narrower screen scope:
ClientContainerPanel.of("inventory-plus:pockets")
    .chrome(() -> List.of(Button.builder()...build()))
    .parity(ScreenMatcher.allExcept(...));
From that declaration the library:
  1. builds the real, synced CreatedSlots on the player's own InventoryMenu (the library-owned MKCInventoryMenuMixin, both sides), with no consumer mixin;
  2. projects the same slots onto every foreign container menu (CreatedSlotProjection, both sides);
  3. gets the creative item picker for free (the creative wrapper wraps whatever CreatedSlots sit on player.inventoryMenu);
  4. on the client, renders the panel's chrome and slot presentation on every container screen its parity scope accepts (default: all).

The client/server split

The server builds a menu's slots at construction, before any client exists, so the slot data is declared here, in common code, and travels onto every container menu unconditionally: the only sync-correct default. What only the client has (the chrome elements and the screen scope, which name client types) is declared with ClientContainerPanel from the client initializer (§0067; the compiler refuses it here). The scope gates presentation, not whether the slot data exists: a slot a screen opts out of is still on that menu, just not shown there. The client wires every registered panel at client start, after every client initializer has run.

    • groupId

      public static SlotGroupId.Created groupId(String containerPanelId, String groupId)
      The SlotGroupId naming one of this panel's slot groups, what a SlotGroupPanelAdapter.onGroup(...) anchors to, so another mod can place a panel against these slots.

      Minted here rather than by hand: the container-parity path derives its own slot panel id (containerPanelId:groupId), so building the identity from the raw ids would silently name a group that never resolves. A slot's address is Address.createdSlot(groupId(panel, group), index).
